metadata.name: Reference CPU 2
metadata.notes:
Reference CPU 2 (docs/reference-cpu-2.md): the reference CPU with eleven more instructions. It can work on single bits (AND, OR, XOR), shift a byte one bit left or right, loop with JNZ, and call a routine and return from it, on a small stack of its own.

Set the speed to 1 kHz or more and press Run. The program in the ROM draws a diagonal line on the screen one pixel at a time, calling the same routine for each of its 32 pixels, and halts with their count on the hex digits.

Select the ROM to read the program in assembly. Its routine, plot, works out which screen byte a pixel is in and which bit, and writes the byte back with that bit set. Most of the added parts are below the read bus: the logic and shift unit, and the stack with its pointer, SP.

props.label: Program
props.source:
; Draws a diagonal line, one pixel at a time: plot is called 32 times.
; RAM: 0 the pixel's column and row, 1 to 3 scratch.

        LDI 0
        STA 0
next:   CALL plot
        LDA 0
        ADI 1
        STA 0
        STA 0xFC        ; HEX: how many so far
        SBI 32
        JNZ next
        LDA 0
        OUT
        HLT

; plot: lights the pixel at column RAM[0], row RAM[0].
plot:   LDA 0
        SHL
        SHL
        SHL
        STA 1           ; row * 8
        LDA 0
        SHR
        SHR
        SHR             ; column / 8
        ADD 1
        STA 0xFE        ; SPTR: the screen byte
        LDA 0
        ANI 7
        STA 2           ; how far right in the byte
        LDI 0x80        ; the leftmost pixel
shift:  STA 3
        LDA 2
        JZ done
        SBI 1
        STA 2
        LDA 3
        SHR
        JMP shift
done:   LDA 3
        OR 0xFD         ; SDATA: the pixels already there
        STA 0xFD
        RET
